newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori undergoes minor mouth surgery.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori undergoes minor mouth surgery.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori will need one week, "more or less," to recover fully from minor surgery on his mouth performed at Lima's top cancer hospital, his daughter said on Monday.
"We are very happy with the operation. ... It is nothing serious," said Keiko Fujimori, who has acted as Peru's first lady since Fujimori split from his wife in 1995.
Speaking to reporters at a charity fund-raising event, she said Fujimori was going ahead with plans to attend her university graduation in the United States next Sunday.
The 58-year-old president spent nine hours on Sunday in Lima's National Institute of Neoplastic Illnesses, which specialises in operations to treat or prevent cancer.
"He is taking it easy this morning. He does not have anything in his agenda," a Government Palace official told Reuters without giving details about the operation.

The leading local newspaper, El Comercio, reported on Monday that Fujimori had been treated for "a small, benign lesion in his vocal cords." Hospital officials said they were still waiting for the results of a biopsy and declined to give more information.
Fujimori, who shows boundless energy in his frequent tours of the provinces and Lima shantytowns, has had a grueling five months handling Peru's hostage crisis and its aftermath.
But last week he obtained permission from Congress for a personal visit to the United States between Thursday and next Tuesday to visit his children studying abroad.
"He is recovering satisfactorily. ... He has to rest for a week. He has been seen here, and he is not going to travel to the United States for another check," Keiko Fujimori said.
Fujimori's former wife, Susana Higuchi, told the local newspaper Sintesis the president had no serious illnesses that she knew of.
